questions.prompt: Which living thing is a common fungus?
questions.explanation: A mushroom is a fungus. It does not make its own food like a green plant.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common fungi in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only examples of fungi?
questions.explanation: Yeast, mould, and mushrooms are common fungi found or used in daily life.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize examples of common fungi.

questions.prompt: Yeast is useful in making dough rise.
questions.explanation: Yeast produces gas during fermentation, and the gas helps dough rise.
questions.learningOutcome: State useful roles of fungi in food preparation.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid eating unknown wild mushrooms?
questions.explanation: Some wild mushrooms can harm people, so unknown fungi should not be eaten.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety precautions when handling or observing fungi.

questions.prompt: What is the role of mould in a compost heap?
options: It helps break down dead matter
It makes clean drinking water instantly
questions.correctAnswer: It helps break down dead matter
questions.explanation: Some fungi decompose dead materials and return nutrients to the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the importance of fungi in nature.

questions.prompt: Which observation best shows that bread has grown mould?
options: Fuzzy coloured patches appear on it
questions.correctAnswer: Fuzzy coloured patches appear on it
questions.explanation: Mould often appears as fuzzy patches on old bread or other food.
questions.learningOutcome: Use observations to identify fungi on materials.

questions.prompt: Name one common fungus that learners may observe in the environment.
questions.explanation: Mushrooms, moulds, puffballs, toadstools, and yeast are examples of fungi.
questions.learningOutcome: Name common fungi found in familiar environments.

questions.prompt: Which safety action is best after touching a sample with mould during a guided activity?
options: Wash hands with soap and water
Place the sample in a desk
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands with soap and water
questions.explanation: Handwashing helps remove germs and spores after handling fungi safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Practise safe handling and disposal of fungi samples.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the economic importance of yeast?
options: It is used in baking and some fermentation processes
It is used to make stones fly
It removes all air from rooms
questions.correctAnswer: It is used in baking and some fermentation processes
questions.explanation: Yeast is useful in food production because it helps dough rise and supports fermentation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the economic importance of useful fungi.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to observe mould growing on food safely. Which plan is best?
options: Use a closed clear container and follow the teacher's instructions
Smell the mould closely every hour
Share the mouldy food at break time
Keep the food open on a classroom desk
questions.correctAnswer: Use a closed clear container and follow the teacher's instructions
questions.explanation: A closed container and teacher guidance reduce contact with spores and spoiled food.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a safe observation activity involving fungi.

questions.prompt: All fungi are harmful to human beings.
questions.explanation: Some fungi are harmful, but others are useful in food production, medicine, and decomposition.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish useful and harmful roles of fungi.

questions.prompt: A group throws mouldy food into an open corner after an investigation. What should they do instead?
options: Dispose of it safely as directed by the teacher
Leave it for other learners to touch
Mix it with clean drinking water
questions.correctAnswer: Dispose of it safely as directed by the teacher
questions.explanation: Safe disposal prevents accidental contact with harmful spores and keeps the environment clean.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safe disposal practices after handling fungi.

questions.prompt: Which animal is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: A snail has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common invertebrates in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which feature is shared by all invertebrates?
options: They do not have a backbone
questions.correctAnswer: They do not have a backbone
questions.explanation: Invertebrates are animals without backbones.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe a general characteristic of invertebrates.

questions.prompt: A butterfly is an invertebrate.
questions.explanation: A butterfly is an insect, and insects are invertebrates.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify common insects as invertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only invertebrates?
questions.explanation: Crabs, spiders, and earthworms lack backbones, unlike the vertebrates in the other groups.
questions.learningOutcome: Group common animals as invertebrates or vertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which invertebrate helps in pollination?
questions.explanation: Bees move pollen from flower to flower, helping many plants make fruits and seeds.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the importance of invertebrates in nature.

questions.prompt: Why are earthworms useful in soil?
options: They help aerate and mix the soil
questions.correctAnswer: They help aerate and mix the soil
questions.explanation: Earthworms make small tunnels and mix organic matter, improving air movement in soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the economic and environmental importance of invertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which sea animal is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: An octopus has no backbone and is classified as a sea invertebrate.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sea invertebrates from examples.

questions.prompt: Which precaution is best when observing a scorpion or unknown spider?
options: Observe from a safe distance with adult guidance
Pick it up with bare hands
Put it in a shirt pocket
questions.correctAnswer: Observe from a safe distance with adult guidance
questions.explanation: Some invertebrates can bite or sting, so learners should observe them safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Practise precautions when handling or observing invertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which invertebrate may transmit malaria parasites between people?
questions.explanation: Some mosquitoes transmit malaria when they bite infected and uninfected people.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how some invertebrates transmit diseases.

questions.prompt: Name one invertebrate that can be found in soil.
questions.explanation: Earthworms, ants, termites, and some larvae are examples of invertebrates found in soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Name common invertebrates in the local environment.

questions.prompt: A learner groups spider, tick, and mite together. What feature makes the grouping sensible?
options: They are invertebrates with jointed legs
questions.correctAnswer: They are invertebrates with jointed legs
questions.explanation: Spiders, ticks, and mites are invertebrates and have jointed legs.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify invertebrates using observable characteristics.

questions.prompt: Which action best protects learners while making an inventory of invertebrates around school?
options: Use observation tools and avoid touching dangerous animals
Put every animal in a pocket
questions.correctAnswer: Use observation tools and avoid touching dangerous animals
questions.explanation: Safe observation protects learners and also avoids harming small animals.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe fieldwork for observing invertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares useful and harmful roles of invertebrates?
options: Some pollinate crops, while others damage crops or spread disease
All invertebrates are safe to hold
Invertebrates only live in the sea
questions.correctAnswer: Some pollinate crops, while others damage crops or spread disease
questions.explanation: Invertebrates have different roles, including pollination, food, soil aeration, pests, and disease transmission.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the importance and risks of invertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through blood vessels.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify main parts of the human circulatory system.

questions.prompt: Which are the main parts of the human circulatory system?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system is made up mainly of the heart, blood, and blood vessels.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify components of the human circulatory system.

questions.prompt: Blood vessels are tubes through which blood flows.
questions.explanation: Blood vessels carry blood to and from different parts of the body.
questions.learningOutcome: State the function of blood vessels.

questions.prompt: Which blood component mainly carries oxygen?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe functions of main blood components.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: White blood cells help protect the body from infection.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain functions of blood components.

questions.prompt: Which blood component helps stop bleeding by clotting blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets help blood clot and reduce bleeding after an injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate blood components to their functions.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels usually carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to other parts of the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe functions of major blood vessels.

questions.prompt: Which habit helps maintain a healthy circulatory system?
questions.explanation: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and improves blood circulation.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose practices that maintain a healthy circulatory system.

questions.prompt: Name one main part of the human circulatory system.
questions.explanation: The heart, blood, and blood vessels are main parts of the circulatory system.
questions.learningOutcome: Name main parts of the circulatory system.

questions.prompt: Why does the pulse become faster after running?
options: The heart pumps faster to supply working muscles
The bones stop supporting the body
questions.correctAnswer: The heart pumps faster to supply working muscles
questions.explanation: During exercise, muscles need more oxygen, so the heart beats faster to move more blood.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate body activity to changes in heartbeat and circulation.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly describes blood flow in a simple circulatory model?
options: Heart pumps blood through vessels to body parts and back
Skin pumps air to roots and back
Stomach pumps stones to the head
Hair carries blood to the soil
questions.correctAnswer: Heart pumps blood through vessels to body parts and back
questions.explanation: Blood moves from the heart through vessels to body tissues and returns to the heart.
questions.learningOutcome: Model the movement of blood in the circulatory system.

questions.prompt: A learner often feels chest pain during activity. What is the most responsible action?
options: Tell a trusted adult and seek health advice
Take unknown tablets from a friend
Run faster to hide the pain
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult and seek health advice
questions.explanation: Chest pain can be serious, so a trusted adult and health worker should help.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose responsible actions for circulatory health concerns.

questions.prompt: Create a simple daily routine that can help a Grade 6 learner maintain a healthy circulatory system.
questions.correctAnswer: A good routine includes regular exercise, balanced meals, enough rest, drinking water, and avoiding harmful substances.
questions.explanation: Healthy routines support the heart, blood vessels, and blood circulation over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a routine plan for maintaining a healthy circulatory system.

questions.prompt: Which change of state happens when ice becomes water?
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid when heat is added.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify changes of state when substances are heated or cooled.

questions.prompt: Which change of state happens when water vapour becomes liquid droplets on a cool lid?
questions.explanation: Condensation changes a gas or vapour into a liquid when it cools.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify condensation in everyday observations.

questions.prompt: Freezing changes a liquid into a solid.
questions.explanation: When water freezes, it changes from liquid water to solid ice.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe freezing as a change of state.

questions.prompt: Which process changes liquid water into water vapour from a wet shirt in sunlight?
questions.explanation: Evaporation changes liquid water into vapour, helping wet clothes dry.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of evaporation in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which example shows sublimation?
options: A solid air freshener slowly changing directly into gas
questions.correctAnswer: A solid air freshener slowly changing directly into gas
questions.explanation: Sublimation is a direct change from solid to gas without first becoming liquid.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sublimation from everyday examples.

questions.prompt: What happens during deposition?
options: A gas changes directly into a solid
A solid changes directly into a gas
A liquid changes into a gas
A solid changes into a liquid
questions.correctAnswer: A gas changes directly into a solid
questions.explanation: Deposition is the reverse of sublimation: gas changes directly into solid.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate deposition from other changes of state.

questions.prompt: Which safety rule is most important when heating wax during a class activity?
options: Hold hot wax with bare hands
Pour hot wax on the floor
questions.explanation: Heating can cause burns or fire, so learners should work carefully with teacher guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety precautions during heating activities.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a change of state with an application?
questions.explanation: Drying cereals uses evaporation as water leaves the grains as vapour.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate changes of state to everyday applications.

questions.prompt: A learner sees steam from hot water forming drops under a cool metal tray. Which two changes are involved?
questions.explanation: Hot water forms vapour by evaporation, then the vapour cools and condenses into droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze linked changes of state in an investigation.

questions.prompt: Name the change of state used when wet clothes dry in the sun.
questions.explanation: Water in the clothes changes into vapour and leaves the fabric.
questions.learningOutcome: Name changes of state in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which fair test can compare evaporation in the sun and in the shade?
options: Place equal amounts of water in similar containers and compare levels later
Use different amounts of water and different containers
Measure one cup today and another next month
Add soil to one cup and oil to another
questions.correctAnswer: Place equal amounts of water in similar containers and compare levels later
questions.explanation: A fair test changes one factor, sunlight, while keeping other conditions similar.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a simple investigation about evaporation.

questions.prompt: Explain how a learner can safely show both evaporation and condensation using hot water and a cool lid.
questions.correctAnswer: Heat water with adult supervision, hold a cool lid above the vapour, and observe droplets forming on the lid.
questions.explanation: The activity shows liquid water becoming vapour, then vapour cooling back to liquid droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a safe investigation showing evaporation and condensation.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up the largest part of air?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in air.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major components of air.

questions.prompt: Which component of air supports burning and breathing?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports burning and is used by living things during respiration.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline uses of different components of air.

questions.prompt: Air is a mixture of gases.
questions.explanation: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour, rare gases, and small particles.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe air as a mixture of gases.

questions.prompt: Which gas do green plants use during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Green plants use carbon dioxide from air to make food during photosynthesis.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate air components to uses by living things.

questions.prompt: Which activity is most likely to cause air pollution near a school?
options: Sweeping with water sprinkled on dust
questions.explanation: Burning plastic releases smoke and harmful gases into the air.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common air pollutants in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which is an effect of air pollution on people?
questions.explanation: Polluted air can irritate the breathing system and make breathing difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain effects of air pollution on health and the environment.

questions.prompt: Which action can reduce dust pollution in a classroom compound?
options: Plant grass and sprinkle water before sweeping
Burn dry leaves beside the door
Break windows to let in dust
questions.correctAnswer: Plant grass and sprinkle water before sweeping
questions.explanation: Vegetation and careful cleaning reduce loose dust in the air.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe methods of reducing air pollution.

questions.prompt: A burning candle is covered with a glass jar and later goes out. What does the activity show?
questions.explanation: The flame goes out when the oxygen inside the jar is used up.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate the presence and use of oxygen in air.

questions.prompt: Name one major gas found in air.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide are examples of gases found in air.
questions.learningOutcome: Name major components of air.

questions.prompt: Which poster message best helps reduce air pollution in a community?
options: Avoid burning waste and plant trees
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid burning waste and plant trees
questions.explanation: Reducing burning and planting trees help keep air cleaner.
questions.learningOutcome: Create messages that promote clean air practices.

questions.prompt: A learner enters a dusty workshop. Which protective items are most suitable?
questions.explanation: A dust mask and goggles reduce inhaling dust and protect the eyes.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety precautions in polluted air environments.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best links air pollution and plant growth?
options: Smoke and harmful gases can damage leaves and reduce healthy growth
Air pollution always makes crops grow faster
Smoke turns all leaves into roots
questions.correctAnswer: Smoke and harmful gases can damage leaves and reduce healthy growth
questions.explanation: Pollutants can block light, damage plant surfaces, and harm normal growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze effects of air pollution on the environment.

questions.prompt: Which material allows most light to pass through clearly?
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent, so light passes through it clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate movement of light through materials.

questions.prompt: What happens to light when it meets a plane mirror?
questions.explanation: A plane mirror reflects light from its smooth surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe reflection of light at plane surfaces.

questions.prompt: Opaque materials block most light from passing through.
questions.explanation: Opaque materials such as wood or cardboard do not let most light pass through.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify materials by how they transmit light.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes light travelling in air during a simple ray activity?
questions.explanation: Ray diagrams use straight lines to show the path of light.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate the movement of light using ray diagrams.

questions.prompt: A shadow forms when an object blocks light. Which object would make the darkest shadow?
questions.explanation: An opaque object blocks light well, so it forms a dark shadow.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain formation of shadows using light movement.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits a plane mirror image?
options: Upright and the same size as the object
questions.correctAnswer: Upright and the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms an upright image that appears the same size as the object.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe characteristics of images formed by plane mirrors.

questions.prompt: Which tool uses plane mirrors to help a person see over or around an obstacle?
questions.explanation: A simple periscope uses mirrors to reflect light to the eye.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of reflection in everyday devices.

questions.prompt: What causes a solar eclipse?
options: The Moon blocks sunlight from reaching part of Earth
Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon
Rain changes into ice in a cloud
questions.correctAnswer: The Moon blocks sunlight from reaching part of Earth
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the Sun and Earth.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate formation of eclipses in nature.

questions.prompt: What causes a lunar eclipse?
options: Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon
The Moon blocks sunlight from reaching Earth
questions.correctAnswer: Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon
questions.explanation: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare solar and lunar eclipses.

questions.prompt: Which condition is needed for a rainbow to form naturally?
options: A stone heated in dry soil
questions.explanation: A rainbow forms when sunlight is bent and separated by water droplets in the air.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe formation of a rainbow in nature.

questions.prompt: Name one transparent material used in a light activity.
questions.explanation: Transparent materials such as clear glass or clear plastic allow light to pass through clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Give examples of materials that transmit light.

questions.prompt: Which safety rule is most important during an eclipse observation?
options: Do not look directly at the Sun
Stare at the Sun without protection
Use a broken mirror close to the eye
questions.correctAnswer: Do not look directly at the Sun
questions.explanation: Looking directly at the Sun can damage the eyes, even during an eclipse.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety precautions during light investigations.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to show reflection using a torch and mirror. Which observation would support the idea?
options: The light beam changes direction after hitting the mirror
The torch turns into a plant
The light becomes a solid stone
questions.correctAnswer: The light beam changes direction after hitting the mirror
questions.explanation: Reflection happens when light bounces off a surface and moves in a new direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze evidence of reflection in a simple experiment.

questions.prompt: Describe how a group can make a simple periscope using locally available materials and two plane mirrors.
questions.correctAnswer: A good design places two plane mirrors at an angle inside a tube so light reflects from the top mirror to the lower mirror and then to the eye.
questions.explanation: A periscope works because plane mirrors reflect light along a changed path.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple device that applies reflection of light.

questions.prompt: Which part of a lever is the turning point?
questions.explanation: The fulcrum or pivot is the point around which a lever turns.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of a lever.

questions.prompt: Which item is a common lever?
questions.explanation: Scissors work as levers because they turn around a pivot to cut materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common levers used in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Levers can make work easier.
questions.explanation: Levers help by changing the size or direction of effort needed to move a load.
questions.learningOutcome: State how levers make work easier.

questions.prompt: In a lever, what is the load?
questions.explanation: The load is the object or resistance that the lever moves.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier.

questions.prompt: Which first-class lever has the fulcrum between the effort and the load?
questions.explanation: A seesaw is a first-class lever because the fulcrum is between the effort and load.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify levers into three classes.

questions.prompt: Which lever is commonly classified as a second-class lever?
questions.explanation: In a wheelbarrow, the load is between the fulcrum at the wheel and the effort at the handles.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify common levers by position of fulcrum, load, and effort.

questions.prompt: Which lever is commonly classified as a third-class lever?
questions.explanation: Tweezers work as third-class levers because the effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify common levers into the three classes.

questions.prompt: What is the effort in a lever?
options: The force applied to move the load
The shadow made by the tool
questions.correctAnswer: The force applied to move the load
questions.explanation: Effort is the force a person or machine applies to make the lever work.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of effort in a lever.

questions.prompt: Name one part of a lever.
questions.explanation: A lever has a fulcrum, a load, and an effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Name parts of a lever.

questions.prompt: A learner moves a heavy stone using a strong stick and a small rock as a pivot. What simple machine is being used?
questions.explanation: The stick turns on a pivot and helps move a load, so it acts as a lever.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate use of levers to make work easier.

questions.prompt: Which choice best improves a beam balance made from local materials?
options: Place the fulcrum at the centre and balance equal loads
Use a weak stick that bends easily
Put both pans on the same side
questions.correctAnswer: Place the fulcrum at the centre and balance equal loads
questions.explanation: A beam balance needs a central pivot and balanced arms to compare loads fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Create and use a simple lever model safely.

questions.prompt: Why should learners keep fingers away from the pivot of scissors during a lever activity?
options: The pivot can pinch or cut fingers
The pivot turns fingers into wood
questions.correctAnswer: The pivot can pinch or cut fingers
questions.explanation: Moving lever parts can pinch or cut, so careful handling prevents injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety precautions when using levers.

questions.prompt: What is another name for a slope used as a simple machine?
questions.explanation: A slope used to make work easier is called an inclined plane.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types of slopes used as simple machines.

questions.prompt: Which example is a slope used to make work easier?
questions.explanation: A ramp is an inclined plane that helps move objects from one level to another.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common slopes in daily life.

questions.prompt: A staircase is an example of a slope used in everyday life.
questions.explanation: A staircase helps people move between different heights, like a series of inclined steps.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize slopes used around school and home.

questions.prompt: How does a gentle ramp help when loading a heavy box into a lorry?
options: It reduces the effort needed by increasing the distance moved
It changes the box into air
It stops the box from moving
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces the effort needed by increasing the distance moved
questions.explanation: A gentle slope spreads the work over a longer distance, so less force is needed at one time.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate how slopes make work easier in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which slope would require the least effort to push the same load upward?
questions.explanation: A longer gentle ramp usually needs less pushing force than a short steep one.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare slopes based on effort needed to move loads.

questions.prompt: Which item works like a wedge, a type of slope?
questions.explanation: A wedge has sloping sides and can separate or cut materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types of slopes used as simple machines.

questions.prompt: Name one place where a slope may be used at school.
questions.explanation: Ramps, staircases, and paths on hills are examples of slopes used around school.
questions.learningOutcome: Give examples of slopes in the local environment.

questions.prompt: Which safety feature is best for a ramp used by learners?
options: A rough non-slip surface and handrail
questions.correctAnswer: A rough non-slip surface and handrail
questions.explanation: A non-slip surface and handrail reduce falls when using a ramp.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety and security when using slopes.

questions.prompt: Why do some roads wind up a hill instead of going straight up?
options: The gentler slope makes climbing easier and safer
Roads cannot be built on hills
The road must avoid all sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: The gentler slope makes climbing easier and safer
questions.explanation: A winding road reduces steepness, making movement uphill easier and safer.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze uses of slopes in everyday life.

questions.prompt: A class wants to test how slope steepness affects effort. Which fair test is best?
options: Use the same toy car and load on ramps of different steepness
Change the load, ramp surface, and car each time
Push one car today and another next term
Measure only the colour of the ramp
questions.correctAnswer: Use the same toy car and load on ramps of different steepness
questions.explanation: A fair test changes slope steepness while keeping the car and load the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an investigation showing how slopes make work easier.

questions.prompt: Which design best helps a wheelchair user enter a classroom built above ground level?
options: A strong gentle ramp with a handrail
A high step with no support
questions.correctAnswer: A strong gentle ramp with a handrail
questions.explanation: A safe ramp improves access by reducing effort and supporting steady movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical slope solutions for school needs.

questions.prompt: Plan a simple slope that learners can use to move a box safely from the ground to a raised platform.
questions.correctAnswer: A good plan uses a strong wide board, gentle angle, rough surface, stable supports, and adult supervision.
questions.explanation: A safe slope reduces effort while preventing slipping, tipping, or injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Make a simple slope for use at school or home using safe materials.
